title: Hydrologic load stress from GNSS did not change the rate of declustered M 2+ California focal-mechanism earthquakes in 2006-2014 or 2015-2025 (elastic half-space load model)
abstract: Question: Johnson, Fu and Burgmann (2017, Science) reported that seasonal water-load stress modulates California microseismicity in 2006-2014: strike-slip events at high shear-stress amplitude (+22.5 % per kPa) and dip-slip events at high shear stressing rate (+12.5 % per kPa/yr). We tested both claims with an independent pipeline in their period and in 2015-2025, which had larger wet and dry years. Approach: we inverted monthly vertical positions from 1,177 NGL GNSS stations for surface water load on a 0.25 degree land grid in an elastic half-space, and calculated the stress at 8 km depth on the preferred plane of 17,214 NCEDC first-motion mechanisms (M 2.0 or more, 34.5-41.5 N, 124.5-117 W, Geysers and Long Valley removed). After nearest-neighbour declustering, 5,673 events remained in 2006-2014 and 6,415 in 2015-2025. We used the NEx statistic and a conditional-logit rate model with month-cluster intervals, placebo phase shifts and an injection test. Results: the strike-slip shear-amplitude slope was -5.1 % per kPa (95% CI -19.5 to +9.3) in 2006-2014 and -1.2 (-14.7 to +12.2) in 2015-2025. The dip-slip shear-rate slope was +0.4 % per kPa/yr (-1.2 to +2.1) and -1.6 (-2.9 to -0.2). Both intervals exclude the published slopes in both periods, and our stress ranges are similar to theirs. Injected published slopes were recovered with power 0.93-1.00. Coulomb amplitude, other planes, M 2.3 or more, Gardner-Knopoff declustering, event depth and 10-times-different load smoothing gave the same result. A weak spring excess in 2006-2014 (Schuster p = 0.022) did not continue in 2015-2025 (p = 0.81). Limitations: our half-space load inversion is smoothed and patchy and is not the layered model of Johnson et al.; stress-model errors can hide a real effect; we used different declustering and the current catalog; we did not test their historical M 5.5+ result.
